thread:
sophia: experimenting with a hybrid approach: fold authz at the edge for concurrent identical model calls, but keep service-account scoping strict. question: when folded, should the auth decision be by the envelope's dominant sa, or per-item sa?

raj: Per-item scoping is safer. If we collapse by dominant sa you can accidentally attribute a request to the wrong SA and break least-privilege. Better: envelope carries per-item sa and a decision_id list. Auth returns an ordered list of allow/deny+quota for each item.

ben: agreed. Also need to decide what the console surface shows. Right now console surface is per-route + per-sa. If we batch, defaults should still be per-sa aggregates but with a visible trace to expand into original items. UX: show "Grouped by fold" banner on any aggregated rows.

sophia: operationally, folding removes a lot of auth RPS but we worry about retries. if the edge retries the envelope, we must avoid double-billing. propose per-item idempotency keys and let billing dedupe on usage_id.

auth-bot: (automated) Policy reminder: token_hash allowed in telemetry; never log raw tokens. See /policy/logging.

raj: for routing: some requests are routed by tenant->regional deployment mapping. If items in a batch map to different regions, we should not fold across region boundaries. Envelope folding only within same routing bucket.

ben: good call. also add a max_item_count and max_payload_bytes cap to avoid big envelopes. fallback to per-request calls when limits hit.

sophia: latency question: folded auth adds an extra decode/expand step in telemetry. Is it okay to make billing async? most customers care about accuracy not immediacy. we'll mirror expanded events to billing during canary to validate.

raj: console drilldown: link expanded events with trace_id and show which decision came from which SA/token_hash (hashed). For compliance, include decision_id -> audit log linkage.

ben: security note: if privacy_mode=redact, we should still emit org/project for billing but redact user-identifiers in the expanded rows. GDPR folks will want that.

sophia: rollout plan: 1% internal traffic -> 1% external canary -> 10% -> 100%. During canaries mirror expansions and compute "billing_delta_percent" and "quota_mismatch_rate". auto-fallback if mismatch > 0.2% for 10m.

raj: i'll draft the envelope proto and the idempotency scheme: idempotency_key = sha256(token_hash + req_id + minute_bucket). include usage_id returned by auth service.

ben: i'll write the console mock and small runbook: where to toggle the edge fold flag and how to search traces by trace_id.

sophia: thanks all. putting up draft PR now. ping #eng-platform when it's ready for review. :thumbsup:
